Definition: a broom (as removing dirt (compare English 'to dust', i.e. remove dust))
BiblicalUsage: The word is a broom, and it appears once, in God's sentence on Babylon: He will sweep the city with the besom of destruction until nothing is left.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the picture is deliberate: the God who made all things can sweep a proud empire away like dust, and no power on earth can stand when He decides to clean house.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
